Even as BASF's financial results suggest that it is resilient in the face of severe natural gas and other input price pressures at its European operations, its outlook remains bleak. There is now little doubt that it will have to shut down operations this winter as part of the EU's energy-saving efforts, with little hope for improvement beyond the winter. The long-term outlook involves probable permanent facility shutdowns in Europe, as well as massive costs of relocating its operations elsewhere, which would likely mean the dividend would have to go at some point. Though BASF stock may look cheap, given that it currently trades at 1/3 of the all-time high price, odds of it rallying from current levels are low while odds of a significant further decline in its stock price are very high. BASF is still a fundamentally solid company, therefore, it might be worth looking at further down the line, once it takes its losses from the ongoing and perhaps permanent EU energy crisis.
